history.summary: Shree Ram Mandir is a local Hindu temple at Rampeth in Jalgaon city (pin 425001), rated ~4.7-4.8/5 across listing sites, described as both a temple and a local tourist attraction. Listings show it ~0.77 km from Jalgaon Junction railway station. No documented history, founder, builder, or antiquity could be found online for this shrine — do not treat it as the famous Ayodhya temple or any historic Ram mandir; it is a city neighbourhood temple whose identity rests on listing data only (UNVERIFIED history).

town_description: Jalgaon is a major city in northern Maharashtra in the Khandesh region, famous for its banana crop, gold trade, cotton and industries. It is the headquarters of Jalgaon district and a rail and road hub connecting central Maharashtra, with well-known regional pilgrim spots such as Padmalaya and the Manudevi temple nearby. The city sits on the Tapi river plain with the Satpura ranges to the north.
